data.title: bn-2f92: commit seal review logs before merge
data.description: For bn-2f92: record the Seal review in the workspace (mark-merged at the approved HEAD, commit only .seal/reviews/<id>) before maw ws merge --destroy. protocol merge/finish emit these steps; docs, managed AGENTS section, worker/dev prompts updated. Lead merge protocol no longer git add -A on a reviewed workspace. risk:medium.

data.body: [severity:medium] Standalone workers now orphan completed work by unconditionally passing --no-merge. This is the non-dispatched branch (dispatched_bone.is_none() at lines 364-365), so unlike the branch above it has no lead guaranteed to consume the workspace. protocol finish deliberately omits mark-merged, the review-log commit, and maw ws merge when --no-merge is set (src/commands/protocol/finish.rs:310-335); this prompt then closes the bone, releases its bone claim, keeps the workspace claim, and stops (lines 377-382). That violates the supported worker-loop contract in AGENTS.md:242-256 and can report a bone done while neither code nor Seal evidence reaches default. Keep --no-merge only for dispatched workers, or establish and verify a lead handoff before closing the bone.

[severity:medium] The primary Seal lifecycle quick reference still tells agents to run mark-merged in default after the workspace merge. That is the exact loss mode this patch fixes: the review exists under the source workspace, and --destroy removes that workspace before default can mark or commit its log. It also directly contradicts the new instructions at AGENTS.md:695-706. Update this command to mark the review and commit .seal/reviews/<id> in $WS before maw ws merge; otherwise agents following the earlier quick reference will continue discarding review evidence.

data.reason: [severity:medium] BLOCK: standalone worker-loop now closes work with --no-merge despite no guaranteed lead handoff, and AGENTS.md still prescribes post-destroy mark-merged in default, reintroducing review-log loss. See threads th-1vwwkq and th-3ebpji. This static Seal review does not satisfy or replace any risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: [severity:high] The new standalone happy path bypasses the risk:critical human-approval gate. It invokes protocol finish first and tells the agent to run every Ready step; the human check at lines 372-375 is only inside the 'If it fails' fallback. protocol finish already fetches BoneInfo (including labels) but keeps only its title (src/commands/protocol/finish.rs:57-70), treats any Seal-approved review as Ready (176-217), and emits/executes mark-merged plus maw ws merge (310-335). Therefore a standalone risk:critical bone with a security LGTM but no authorized human approval reaches default through the normal successful path. Move this check before the protocol call and enforce it in protocol finish/merge from the bone labels and configured approver evidence; prompt-only fallback text is not an authorization control. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: critical code merges without the required human; (2) detection: audit merged risk:critical bones for a verified approval message/comment and emit a protocol diagnostic when absent; (3) rollback: stop push/release, use maw undo or revert the merge, then re-run approval; (4) invalidating dependency: the current design assumes protocol finish enforces the same gate as the fallback, but it does not; (5) least-certain assumption: how an authorized human approval is represented and identity-checked must be made explicit and machine-verifiable.

[severity:medium] This closes the review before the destructive merge has actually succeeded, leaving no safe gate after a late conflict. The preflight explicitly proceeds when --check fails or is unparseable (lines 620-625), and the target can also change between preflight and merge. If maw ws merge then records conflicts, resolving them changes HEAD, yet src/templates/docs/merge-check.md:38-51 tells the operator to bypass edict protocol merge and retry maw ws merge directly because the review is already merged. That can merge conflict-resolution code which no reviewer approved. Keep the review recoverable until a conflict-free merge is guaranteed, or require a fresh review after any code-changing retry; a raw retry is safe only when the non-.seal tree is proven identical to the approved target and the sole extra commit is the review log.

data.reason: Blocking target 9301085708b75d6b92c15a26030180991d48447f: standalone protocol finish bypasses the risk:critical human-approval gate, and post-mark-merged conflict recovery can merge unreviewed resolution commits via a raw retry.

data.body: Fixed in cef59e9e: the worker prompt runs the human-approval check before any finish path. protocol finish and protocol merge now fail closed on a risk:critical bone (Blocked, no merge steps, --force does not lift it), so a security LGTM alone never reaches the merge. Machine-verifiable approval evidence is a separate design question; the gate stays closed until a human merges manually.

Fixed in cef59e9e: merge-check.md and the protocol merge conflict-recovery diagnostic now allow a direct retry only when the resolution changes nothing outside .seal/ and .bones/. Any other resolution needs a commit, a fresh review for the bone, and a new protocol merge.

[severity:high] The reviewed-commit gate still admits unreviewed working-tree additions and deletions. `seal reviews mark-merged` checks the approval against HEAD, and the path-limited review-log commit leaves every other dirty path uncommitted; `maw ws merge` then snapshots the source workspace, including untracked additions and tracked deletions. Thus an add/delete made after LGTM leaves HEAD unchanged, passes mark-merged, and lands in default through either protocol merge or protocol finish --execute. The advisory status check in the dev-loop prompt does not protect these executable paths. Before mark-merged, fail closed unless the only dirty paths are the exact `.seal/reviews/<review-id>/` metadata being recorded, and apply that shared check to finish and merge. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: arbitrary unreviewed files can be added or reviewed files deleted in default; (2) detection: capture and reject `git status --porcelain` entries outside the exact review-log directory, then audit the merged tree against the approved commit plus that log; (3) rollback: stop push/release and `maw undo` or revert the merge, remove the dirty delta, and obtain a fresh LGTM; (4) invalidating dependency: this design assumes maw merges committed HEAD only, but maw merge snapshots workspace changes; (5) least-certain assumption: dirty rename/modify handling varies by path state, but untracked additions and tracked deletions are sufficient to reproduce the bypass.

[severity:high] The new risk:critical guard is bypassable whenever the caller makes the bone association unavailable. `find_bone_for_workspace` only accepts a bone corroborated by claims held under the supplied `--agent`; with no such claim (or a different agent identity), this branch proceeds without a bone. Passing `--force` then skips the review gate and emits the merge steps, so the later label check at lines 301-321 never sees `risk:critical` despite the new promise that --force cannot lift it. Fail closed when the bone cannot be identified under --force, or bind the workspace to its bone through an independent immutable source and check that bone label before honoring force. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: a critical workspace reaches default without authorized human approval; (2) detection: emit a hard diagnostic for force plus an unresolved bone and audit forced merges against workspace/bone claims and critical labels; (3) rollback: stop push/release, `maw undo` or revert the merge, restore the claim/binding, and obtain human approval; (4) invalidating dependency: the guard assumes the current caller still holds the bone claim, but claims are advisory and can be released or queried under another identity; (5) least-certain assumption: the normal lead path may retain the claim, but the public force path explicitly supports degraded state and remains directly reachable.

[severity:medium] Not fully fixed. The new protocol diagnostic and merge-check.md distinguish `.seal/`/`.bones/`-only retries from code-changing resolutions, but the canonical finish workflow still says to restore `.bones/ .agents/ .claude/` and retry the merge directly (`src/templates/docs/finish.md:71-79`, rendered at `.agents/edict/finish.md:71-79`) with no fresh-review condition. Because finish now marks the review merged before the merge attempt, an agent following that fallback can change security-relevant workflow/hook content after approval and bypass the stated re-review requirement. Make finish.md use the same `.seal/`/`.bones/` exception and require a fresh review for `.agents/`, `.claude/`, or any other changed path.

[severity:high] The standalone `protocol finish` path now checks `risk:critical` before emitting merge steps, so that part is fixed. The human gate is not yet preserved across the lead merge path: an unresolved claim-derived bone association proceeds at `src/commands/protocol/merge.rs:287-292`, and `--force` then skips the review gate and the label is never loaded. See thread th-1jjmub for the file-backed bypass and required fix.

data.reason: Two high-severity approval-gate bypasses remain: Maw can snapshot unreviewed dirty additions/deletions after LGTM (th-2lpf48), and protocol merge --force can skip the risk:critical guard when the claim-derived bone association is unavailable (th-1jjmub). Conflict-recovery guidance also remains inconsistent in finish.md (th-36axv2).

data.body: Fixed in e4237e75: the first record step, emitted by protocol merge and finish, fails unless git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all lists nothing outside .seal/reviews/<id>. All manual record sequences (docs, prompts, AGENTS.md) carry the same check. Confirmed that maw merges uncommitted adds and deletes; the check refuses both. A unit test runs every emitted step through sh -n.

Fixed: finish.md, merge-check.md and the protocol merge diagnostic now say that after the review is recorded only .bones/ may be restored for a direct retry; any .agents/, .claude/ or other change needs a fresh review.

Split to bn-3cc4 by user decision: the --force policy (fail closed on an unresolved bone vs an immutable workspace-to-bone binding) is a separate policy change. This patch adds the risk:critical gate where none existed; main has no critical check on this path at all.
The protocol finish path is fixed. The remaining lead --force path is th-1jjmub, split to bn-3cc4.

A distinct post-check mutation window remains and is filed separately.

data.body: [severity:high] Still blocking at e4237e751a76197a2e57f9f87e22af2ac13c0f74. Splitting remediation to another bone does not preserve the current risk:critical gate required by this review. merge.rs:198-201 derives the association from advisory claims; merge.rs:287-292 proceeds when it is absent; and merge.rs:214-216 skips the review gate under --force. The public force path therefore emits merge steps without ever loading the critical label. The five failure-mode answers in th-1jjmub.1 remain current.

[severity:high] The dirty-tree guard is not bound to the tree Maw eventually snapshots. This first step checks once, then lines 521-525 run mark-merged and a Git commit, and only afterwards do finish.rs and merge.rs invoke maw ws merge. A commit hook or concurrent workspace writer can add an untracked file or delete a tracked file after this check; Maw collect snapshots the live working tree and merges those additions/deletions even though Seal approved only the earlier HEAD. Re-checking in a later standalone step still leaves a race: bind the approved commit plus exact review-log commit to the Maw input, make Maw merge committed content only, or hold an enforceable workspace lock across validation and snapshot. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: arbitrary post-LGTM additions or deletions land in default; (2) detection: compare the frozen merge input tree and live dirty-path inventory with the approved target plus the exact review-log delta, and alert on any other path; (3) rollback: stop push/release, use maw undo or revert the merge, remove the unreviewed delta, and obtain a fresh LGTM; (4) invalidating dependency: the guard assumes no hook or writer changes the workspace between status and Maw snapshot, but the commands are separate and no lock enforces that; (5) least-certain assumption: ordinary agents may not configure mutating commit hooks, but concurrent workspace writes remain possible and the security property currently depends on their absence.

data.reason: [severity:high] BLOCK on e4237e751a76197a2e57f9f87e22af2ac13c0f74. The lead merge --force path can bypass the risk:critical human-approval guard when the claim-derived bone association is unavailable (th-1jjmub), and the one-time dirty-tree check is not atomically bound to Maw live snapshot, allowing post-check unreviewed additions or deletions to merge (th-2b1rae). Fixed earlier findings were verified and resolved. This static Seal verdict does not replace the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: Narrowed in 8c3bdc30: the merge step is now '<clean check> && maw ws merge ...' in one shell command, emitted by protocol merge and finish and used by every manual sequence. Verified in a scratch repo: a late untracked file makes it refuse and leaves the workspace; a clean tree merges. The remaining window is inside maw's own snapshot and edict cannot close it. Filed maw bn-31u8 for a committed-only / exact-commit merge; edict will pass it once it exists. User decision: accept this residual window until then.

Fixed in 249bc467 by user decision: protocol merge --force now blocks when it cannot load the bone (no linked bone, or bn show fails), so --force can never emit merge steps without the risk:critical label check. Tests: check_bone_gate_force_blocks_missing_bone, check_bone_gate_force_blocks_unresolvable_bone.

[severity:high] Still blocking at 8c3bdc3090ea49c7182364668d2a8e856b853388. The new None and bn-show error checks do not prove that the loaded bone belongs to the supplied workspace. `find_bone_for_workspace` at src/commands/protocol/merge.rs:888-892 returns the callers sole held bone for any workspace name; `execute` at lines 198-216 then checks that unrelated bones labels and skips review under `--force`. The existing test at lines 1275-1280 even resolves `my-ws` to `bn-mine` solely from that one bone claim. Therefore an agent holding one benign bone can run protocol merge for a different risk:critical workspace with --force, load only the benign labels, and receive merge steps without human approval. Require an association that binds this exact workspace to this exact bone, or under force accept only an exact workspace-name plus held-bone match and reject the single-claim fallback. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: critical code reaches default without authorized human approval; (2) detection: reject and log workspace/bone mismatches and audit every forced merge against an exact association; (3) rollback: stop push or release, run `maw undo` or revert, restore the correct binding, and obtain human approval; (4) invalidating dependency: exclusive ownership of a bone claim does not associate an arbitrary workspace with that bone; (5) least-certain assumption: normal automation often names a workspace after its bone, but the public CLI accepts any existing workspace and this fallback ignores its name.

[severity:high] Still blocking at 8c3bdc3090ea49c7182364668d2a8e856b853388. The executable protocol path narrows the race, but official manual paths still omit the final check. `.agents/edict/merge-check.md:67-71` and `src/templates/docs/merge-check.md:67-71` perform a separate status check and review-log commit, then invoke a plain merge. `src/templates/docs/worker-loop.md:176-182` first shows an ellipsis-only checked command, then directs the actual teardown through a second plain merge command. A hook or concurrent writer can add or delete a source file after the earlier check and have Maw snapshot it unreviewed. Make every actual reviewed merge command carry the final check, and remove the duplicate unchecked command. Five failure-mode answers: (1) production failure: unreviewed additions or deletions land in default through the documented fallback; (2) detection: compare the final Maw input tree and dirty inventory with the approved target plus the exact committed review log; (3) rollback: stop push or release, use `maw undo` or revert, remove the unreviewed delta, and obtain a fresh LGTM; (4) invalidating dependency: the docs assume no writer changes the workspace between separate commands; (5) least-certain assumption: agents may prefer protocol mode, but these fallbacks are explicitly authoritative when the protocol is unavailable.

[severity:medium] The clean guard treats failure to inspect the workspace as a clean result. `test -z "$(maw exec ... git status ...)"` observes only stdout; if `maw exec` or `git status` exits nonzero with empty stdout, `test -z` succeeds and the chained merge runs. Since this is a security gate, capture the status output only after a successful command, for example `out=$(maw exec ... git status ...) || exit; test -z "$out" ...`, so inspection errors fail closed. Add a test that substitutes a failing status command and proves the merge side is not reached.

data.reason: Two high-severity merge-gate bypasses remain: --force can bind an arbitrary workspace to the callers sole benign bone claim, and documented manual workflows still perform reviewed merges without the final same-command clean check. The clean guard also fails open when status inspection errors.

data.body: Fixed in e671b6ef: the check is now '{ out=$(maw exec ... git status ...) && test -z "$out" || { echo ...; false; }; }', so a failed status stops the merge. Test reviewed_merge_fails_closed_when_status_fails puts a fake maw on PATH: status exit 1 never reaches the merge, status exit 0 with no output does.

Fixed in e671b6ef: every documented reviewed merge (finish.md step 8 and retries, worker-loop.md teardown, merge-check.md steps 2, recovery 5 and manual 5, managed AGENTS section, dev and worker prompts) is now the single '<fail-closed check> && maw ws merge' command; the duplicate unchecked command is gone. The protocol's conflict-retry guidance reruns edict protocol merge before recording and uses the checked merge after. The residual window inside maw's snapshot is tracked in maw bn-31u8.

Fixed in e671b6ef: under --force, find_bone_for_workspace takes an exact binding only (claim memo, or a workspace named after a held bone); the sole-bone-claim fallback is off, so an unrelated benign claim yields no bone and --force blocks. Test exact_lookup_ignores_a_sole_unrelated_bone_claim.

data.body: [severity:high] The generated primary lead workflow still bypasses every gate added by this range. Lines 115-118 tell a lead merging a completed worker workspace to run bare `maw ws merge`; the same unqualified command also appears in the top-level change recipe at line 8 and workspace quick reference at line 94. On a reviewed workspace this neither marks and commits the Seal log nor runs the final dirty-tree guard, and on a `risk:critical` workspace it never invokes protocol merge, loads the bone label, or verifies the separate human approval. A lead following the shorter authoritative recipe can therefore discard review evidence, merge post-LGTM additions/deletions, and bypass the critical gate despite the safer recipe added later at lines 214-229. Route these recipes through `edict protocol merge` and its emitted steps, or make every reviewed merge recipe carry the record/check sequence and explicitly preserve the critical manual-approval path. Five risk answers: (1) failure modes: reviewed or critical worker code reaches default without durable Seal evidence, without review freshness/dirty-tree enforcement, or without human approval; (2) edge cases: the bypass is repeated at lines 8 and 94 and applies whether the omitted review log is merely lost or the live workspace also has uncommitted adds/deletes; (3) rollback: stop push/release, use `maw undo` or revert, recover the workspace if destroyed, restore the review log, obtain a fresh LGTM and any required human approval, then merge through the gated path; (4) monitoring: flag direct reviewed `maw ws merge --destroy` invocations lacking a preceding current `mark-merged` plus exact review-log commit, and audit merged risk:critical bones for the recorded approval anchor; (5) validation: render AGENTS.md from this template and prove every merge recipe either delegates to protocol merge or executes the same fail-closed record/check sequence, including a reviewed dirty workspace and a risk:critical workspace.
